blocks.text: Imagine a blueprint for a house. This blueprint defines the structure, but it isn't a house itself. Similarly, in programming, a class is a blueprint for creating objects.

blocks.markdown: In object-oriented programming, a class is a blueprint for creating objects (instances). A class defines a type by bundling data and methods that operate on that data. This approach helps manage complexity in large programs by encapsulating state and behavior.

blocks.title: Class
blocks.text: A class is a user-defined data type that serves as a blueprint for objects. It defines attributes (fields) and methods (functions) that operate on these attributes.

blocks.markdown:
### Defining a Class
To define a class in a programming language like Python, you use the `class` keyword followed by the class name. Inside the class, you define fields and methods. A field is a variable that holds data, and a method is a function that operates on the data.

blocks.caption: Basic structure of a class in Python

blocks.title: Creating a Simple Class
blocks.prompt: Define a class `Car` with a field `color` and a method `drive`.

steps.text: Start by defining the class with the `class` keyword.
Add the constructor method `__init__` to initialize the `color` field.
steps.latex: class Car:\newline\quad def __init__(self, color):\newline\quad\quad self.color = color

steps.text: Define the `drive` method that outputs a message.
steps.latex: def drive(self):\newline\quad print('The car is driving.')

blocks.markdown:
### Instances of a Class
An instance is a specific object created from a class. Each instance can have different values for its fields, but it shares the same methods defined by the class.

blocks.title: Creating an Instance
blocks.prompt: Create an instance of the `Car` class with the color 'red'.

steps.text: Use the class name followed by parentheses to create an instance.
Pass the color 'red' to the constructor.

blocks.title: Instance vs. Class
blocks.text: A class is a blueprint, while an instance is a concrete object created from that blueprint. Each instance has its own state, defined by its fields.

blocks.markdown:
### The `self` Keyword
In class methods, `self` refers to the instance calling the method. It allows access to the instance's fields and other methods.
